title: perf(canary): automated detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Priya Shah
description: Summary: Adds an automated detection pipeline for performance canaries that identifies statistically-significant latency and throughput regressions and enforces rollout guards to prevent bad model or serving changes from reaching production. Motivation: we've seen a number of regressions slip through manual canary reviews when signal is noisy and teams are stretched; this change reduces human toil and enforces consistent rollback behavior. What I changed: 1) New detector module (perf/canary/detector.py) implementing a sequential hypothesis test based on bootstrapped latency distributions and a lightweight nonparametric test for throughput shifts; detector supports configurable alpha, sample windows, and expected-effect-size thresholds. 2) Canary engine integration: canary-runner now emits per-batch metrics to the detector and receives a decision (ok/warn/fail) which gates rollout stages. 3) Rollout guards: declarative rollout policy in perf/canary/policies.yaml with automatic pause, rollback, and notification hooks (Console banner + pager duty trigger) when the detector reports fail. 4) Console updates: new Canary Health view and signal visualizations (redwood-console/src/components/CanaryView.tsx). 5) Integration tests and synthetic workload generator (tests/perf/canary_integration_test.py) plus end-to-end smoke in the perf-canary CI job. 6) Helm chart values and secret handling for private deployments (infra/helm/perf-canary-chart/values.yaml). Migration notes: new cluster role permissions for canary metrics ingestion and a small DB migration to store detector state (idempotent). Risk mitigation: detector defaults to conservative alpha=0.01 and requires a minimum sample window; rollout policy defaults to manual for existing customers and auto-enforced for canary-enabled release channels. Related work: follows design doc ENG-3245 and ties into the perf-canary observability dashboards. Testing: unit tests for detector logic, canary-runner integration tests against synthetic traffic, and staged rollout on staging cluster for 48 hours. Rollout plan: feature-flagged and progressive enablement across teams. Contact: @priyash for follow-ups.

review_comments: Ava Li: Nice work. Can you clarify how the detector handles transient spikes (single-batch outliers)? It looks like the sample window is fixed -- suggest adding EWMA smoothing or outlier trimming.
Priya Shah: Added a configurable outlier_trimming parameter and an EWMA prefilter; documentation updated in docs/perf/canary-automation.md.
Marcus Nguyen: We should be careful about the default alpha for auto-rollout. Can we keep manual by default and enable auto for perf-enabled channels only?
Priya Shah: Agreed. Default policy remains manual; auto enforcement is opt-in per release channel. Added policy defaults to policies.yaml and a migration check that prevents accidental enablement.
Samir Patel: CI flaky on the first run, e2e perf job failed due to timing of synthetic generator. Re-ran and all checks passed. Please add retries to the job to reduce flakiness.
Priya Shah: Added retry/backoff to ci/jobs/perf-canary.yml and increased synthetic generator warmup time by 20%.
Ava Li: Approving after addressing comments. Left one minor nit about log level for decision events (info -> debug).
Priya Shah: Switched decision events to debug behind a feature flag; default retains info for first 24h of rollout as discussed.
release_notes: Adds automated canary detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions. Feature-flagged; defaults to manual rollouts. Admins must grant canary ingestion RBAC. See docs/perf/canary-automation.md for configuration and migration steps.
notes_short: Automated perf canary detection + rollout guards; conservative defaults; feature-flagged rollout.
